title: Getting Started with geomattR
text: geomattR provides tools compute geometric attributes spatial polygons. default, core spatial calculations use geodesic core measurements (method "geo", recommended), also support "haversine" "cosine" methods. studies covering large countries, continents world, geodesic calculations unprojected polygons (WGS84) improve accuracy minimize shape distortion.

title: Getting Started with geomattR
text: Install geomattR GitHub:
code: # Install if you haven't already # install.packages("devtools") # devtools::install_github("gortegasolis/geomattR")  library(geomattR) library(terra)

title: Getting Started with geomattR
text: main function calculate_geometric_attributes(), takes SpatVector polygons returns object added geometric attribute columns:
code: # Create a simple polygon (1x1 degree square at equator) coords <- cbind(c(0, 0, 1, 1, 0), c(0, 1, 1, 0, 0)) polygon <- vect(coords, type = "polygon", crs = "EPSG:4326")  # Calculate all available metrics result <- calculate_geometric_attributes(polygon)  # View the results print(result)  # Or view specific columns print(result[, c("area", "perimeter", "compactness")])

title: Getting Started with geomattR
text: GeomattR calculates 20 different geometric metrics organized several categories:

title: Getting Started with geomattR
code: # Calculate area and perimeter polygon_with_size <- calculate_geometric_attributes(   polygon,   metrics = c("area", "perimeter", "hole_area", "hole_area_pct") )  # Area in square meters (using geodesic calculations) print(polygon_with_size$area)  # Perimeter in meters print(polygon_with_size$perimeter)

title: Getting Started with geomattR
code: # Calculate shape characteristics polygon_with_shape <- calculate_geometric_attributes(   polygon,   metrics = c(     "compactness", # Polsby-Popper (0-1, 1=perfect circle)     "reock", # Reock compactness     "shape_index", # Dimensionless shape complexity     "circularity_ratio", # Based on max length     "fractaldimension", # Boundary complexity     "elongation_rectangle" # mean(long sides) / mean(short sides) from the minimum bounding rectangle   ) )  # Perfect circle has compactness = 1 # Irregular shapes have lower values print(polygon_with_shape[, c("compactness", "shape_index")])

title: Getting Started with geomattR
code: # Calculate orientation polygon_with_orient <- calculate_geometric_attributes(   polygon,   metrics = c("bearing", "northerness", "ew_length", "ns_length", "maxlength") )  # Bearing: axial orientation of the maximum length line, always measured # south to north, so it lies within [-90, 90] (0 = N-S axis, -90/90 = E-W axis) print(polygon_with_orient$bearing)  # Northerness: cosine of bearing (0 = E-W axis, 1 = N-S axis) print(polygon_with_orient$northerness)  # Extents in meters: maximum distances from East to West and North to South print(paste("EW Extent:", round(polygon_with_orient$ew_length, 0), "m")) print(paste("NS Extent:", round(polygon_with_orient$ns_length, 0), "m"))

title: Getting Started with geomattR
code: polygon_with_complexity <- calculate_geometric_attributes(   polygon,   metrics = c("sinuosity", "fractaldimension") )  # Sinuosity: perimeter / max_length (>1 indicates rougher boundary) print(polygon_with_complexity$sinuosity)  # Fractal dimension (FRAGSTATS convention): boundary complexity, approaching # 1 for simple square-like shapes and 2 for highly convoluted boundaries print(polygon_with_complexity$fractaldimension)

title: Getting Started with geomattR
code: # Get centroid coordinates and structure info polygon_with_geom <- calculate_geometric_attributes(   polygon,   metrics = c(     "decimallongitude",     "decimallatitude",     "num_holes",     "num_polygons"   ) )  print(polygon_with_geom[, c("decimallongitude", "decimallatitude")])

title: Getting Started with geomattR
text: multiple polygons, calculate_geometric_attributes() processes sequentially:
code: # Create multiple polygons coords1 <- cbind(c(0, 0, 1, 1, 0), c(0, 1, 1, 0, 0)) coords2 <- cbind(c(1, 1, 2, 2, 1), c(1, 2, 2, 1, 1))  poly1 <- vect(coords1, type = "polygon", crs = "EPSG:4326") poly2 <- vect(coords2, type = "polygon", crs = "EPSG:4326")  # Combine into single SpatVector polygons <- rbind(poly1, poly2)  # Calculate metrics for all polygons at once results <- calculate_geometric_attributes(   polygons,   metrics = c("area", "perimeter", "compactness") )  # Results have same row count as input print(nrow(results)) # 2  # All metrics calculated print(results[, c("area", "perimeter", "compactness")])

title: Getting Started with geomattR
text: large datasets many polygons, use cl argument calculate_geometric_attributes() run calculations parallel:
code: library(parallel)  # Create multiple polygons polygons <- rbind(poly1, poly2) # From previous example  # Set up cluster n_cores <- detectCores() - 1 cl <- makeCluster(n_cores)  # Process in parallel using the main function results <- calculate_geometric_attributes(   polygons,   metrics = "all",   cl = cl )  # Clean up stopCluster(cl)  # Results should be equivalent to sequential processing # (allowing for tiny floating-point differences) print(head(results))

title: Getting Started with geomattR
text: GeomattR automatically handles different coordinate systems. default, core spatial calculations prioritize geodesic core measurements (method "geo", recommended). However, distance-based calculations, helper functions (calc_extent() calc_elongation()) accept method parameter can changed "haversine" "cosine". details distance methods behave, refer method descriptions terra package. Automatic CRS conversion handles execution details:
code: # Create polygon in geographic CRS (WGS84/EPSG:4326) poly_geographic <- vect(coords1, type = "polygon", crs = "EPSG:4326")  # Create same polygon in projected CRS (UTM Zone 30N) poly_projected <- project(poly_geographic, "EPSG:32630")  # Calculate metrics on both result_geo <- calculate_geometric_attributes(poly_geographic, metrics = "area") result_proj <- calculate_geometric_attributes(poly_projected, metrics = "area")  # Both should give similar results (using geodesic calculations by default) print(paste("Geographic CRS area:", round(result_geo$area, 0), "m²")) print(paste("Projected CRS area:", round(result_proj$area, 0), "m²"))  # Difference should be minimal due to default geodesic calculations print(paste(   "Difference:",   round(abs(result_geo$area - result_proj$area), 0),   "m²" ))

title: Calculate Geometric Attributes of Spatial Polygons
text: Honestly, use developing package way learn spatial indices decomposing formulas explaining work writing documentation. geomattR provides comprehensive toolkit calculating geometric morphometric attributes spatial polygons. computes area, perimeter, compactness, elongation, orientation, fractal dimension, various shape indices. package particularly useful : - Geospatial analysts analyzing shape size geographic features - Urban planners characterizing building neighborhood geometry - Environmental scientists studying habitat patch metrics - Remote sensing practitioners extracting morphological features vector data - Landscape ecologists quantifying landscape structure - Political scientists examining electoral district shapes - Epidemiologists analyzing spatial spread patterns Core spatial calculations use terra package efficient spatial data handling geodesic measurement support, geosphere used bearing estimation metric requires geographic coordinates. Distance- area-based metrics computed, shape indices derived quantities.

title: Calculate Geometric Attributes of Spatial Polygons
text: area: Total area square meters. perimeter: Total perimeter length meters. hole_area: Total area interior holes square meters. hole_area_pct: Percentage gross polygon area (including holes) occupied holes: HA%=hole_areaarea+hole_area×100HA\% = \frac{\text{hole\_area}}{\text{area} + \text{hole\_area}} \times 100.

title: Calculate Geometric Attributes of Spatial Polygons
text: compactness: Polsby-Popper compactness, circularity index compares polygon area area circle perimeter: C=4πAP2C = \frac{4\pi }{P^2}. Values closer 1 indicate compact (circle-like) shapes. reock: Reock compactness, defined polygon area relative area minimum enclosing circle: R=AAMECR = \frac{}{A_{MEC}}. Values closer 1 indicate polygon fills enclosing circle efficiently. elongation_rectangle: Elongation index minimum bounding rectangle convex hull. current implementation, computed mean two largest side lengths divided mean two shortest side lengths: E=mean(long sides)mean(short sides)E = \frac{\text{mean}(\text{long sides})}{\text{mean}(\text{short sides})}. shape_index: Dimensionless irregularity index comparing polygon perimeter perimeter circle area: SI=P2πASI = \frac{P}{2\sqrt{\pi }}. value 1 corresponds perfect circle; larger values indicate increasing irregularity. circularity_ratio: Circularity index based area maximum hull distance: CR=4AπLmax⁡2CR = \frac{4A}{\pi L_{\max}^2}. fractaldimension: Perimeter-area scaling index boundary complexity following FRAGSTATS convention: D=2ln⁡(0.25P)ln⁡()D = \frac{2\ln(0.25P)}{\ln()}. Approaches 1 simple (square-like) shapes 2 highly convoluted boundaries.

title: Calculate Geometric Attributes of Spatial Polygons
text: bearing: Axial orientation maximum length line, measured geographic bearing southernmost northernmost point, decimal degrees (−90∘-90^{\circ} 90∘90^{\circ}). line always oriented south--north, describes orientation axis, travel direction: −90∘-90^{\circ}/ 90∘90^{\circ} east-west, 0∘0^{\circ} north-south. northerness: Cosine bearing: N=cos⁡(bearing×π180)N = \cos(\text{bearing} \times \frac{\pi}{180}) (ranges 0 1; 1 = north-south axis, 0 = east-west axis). ew_length: Average east-west extent meters: EW=d(NW,NE)+d(SW,SE)2EW = \frac{d(NW, NE) + d(SW, SE)}{2}. ns_length: Average north-south extent meters: NS=d(SW,NW)+d(SE,NE)2NS = \frac{d(SW, NW) + d(SE, NE)}{2}. maxlength: Maximum distance across convex hull: Lmax=max⁡pi,pjd(pi,pj)L_{\max} = \max_{p_i, p_j} d(p_i, p_j).

title: Calculate Geometric Attributes of Spatial Polygons
text: num_holes: Number interior holes (rings). num_polygons: Number separate polygon parts (multi-part count). decimallongitude: Centroid longitude decimal degrees. decimallatitude: Centroid latitude decimal degrees. sinuosity: Perimeter--diameter proxy (perimeter divided maximum hull distance): S=PLmaxS = \frac{P}{L_{\max}}.

title: Calculate Geometric Attributes of Spatial Polygons

Area, perimeter, extent, maximum distance, bearing computed according selected method. Derived shape indices (example compactness, sinuosity, fractaldimension) calculated base quantities. details methods geo, haversine cosine, please refer documentation terra package.

title: Calculate Polygon Extent — calc_extent
text: Extent computed bounding box polygon's convex hull. Southwest (SW), Southeast (SE), Northwest (NW), Northeast (NE) corners box evaluated using terra::distance() selected method. metric values calculated : East-West Extent: average length top bottom bounding box edges: $$\text{EW} = \frac{d(SW, SE) + d(NW, NE)}{2}$$ North-South Extent: average length left right bounding box edges: $$\text{NS} = \frac{d(SW, NW) + d(SE, NE)}{2}$$ method "geo" "haversine", hull projected EPSG:4326 needed distance calculations. output = "value": direction = "ew": returns east-west extent (numeric scalar) direction = "ns": returns north-south extent (numeric scalar) direction = c("ew", "ns") (order): returns values named numeric vector output = "polygon", requested extent columns added attributes. interpretation relation shape metrics, see calculate_geometric_attributes.

title: Calculate Polygon Extent — calc_extent
code: library(terra) coords <- cbind(c(0, 0, 1, 1, 0), c(0, 1, 1, 0, 0)) polygon <- vect(coords, type = "polygon", crs = "EPSG:4326")  # Get one extent value ew_extent <- calc_extent(polygon, direction = "ew")  # Get both extent values both_extents <- calc_extent(polygon, direction = c("ns", "ew"))  # Return polygon with only requested extent columns polygon_with_ew <- calc_extent(polygon, direction = "ew", output = "polygon")  # Return polygon with both extent columns polygon_with_extents <- calc_extent(polygon, output = "polygon")  # Use a custom distance method supported by terra::distance() extents_planar <- calc_extent(polygon, direction = c("ew", "ns"), method = "cosine")

text: input SpatVector additional columns containing requested geometric attributes: area: Total area square meters. Wrapper around terra::expanse(). perimeter: Total perimeter length meters. Wrapper around terra::perim(). compactness: Polsby-Popper compactness. reock: Reock compactness. elongation_rectangle: Elongation index minimum bounding rectangle. num_holes: Number holes (interior rings) polygon. hole_area: Total area holes square meters. hole_area_pct: Percentage total area occupied holes. num_polygons: Number separate polygon parts (multi-part count). ew_length: East-west extent meters. ns_length: North-south extent meters. maxlength: Maximum Feret distance across convex hull. bearing: Axial orientation maximum length line: geographic bearing southernmost northernmost point decimal degrees, within [-90, 90] (0 = north-south, -90/90 = east-west). northerness: Cosine bearing, within [0, 1] (1 = north-south axis, 0 = east-west axis). fractaldimension: Boundary complexity index (FRAGSTATS convention). sinuosity: Perimeter--maximum-length ratio. shape_index: Dimensionless irregularity index. circularity_ratio: Circularity index based area maximum hull distance. decimallongitude: Centroid longitude decimal degrees. decimallatitude: Centroid latitude decimal degrees.

title: Calculate Geometric Attributes of Spatial Polygons — calculate_geometric_attributes
text: polygon processed independently via internal function .calculate_geometric_attributes_single, handle single feature time, optimized ensure intermediate objects required multiple metrics (convex hull, minimum circle, etc.) computed per feature. Sequential vs. Parallel: cl = NULL (default), features processed sequentially lapply. cl valid cluster, features distributed across workers via parLapply. function handles library loading function export cluster automatically. Geodesic Measurements: function supports methods "geo" (default), "haversine" "cosine" (less precise faster great-circle approximations). three lon/lat great-circle methods terra::distance(); projected CRS method ignored distances Cartesian. Inputs internally projected EPSG:4326 metric requires geographic coordinates restored original CRS return applicable. Scope method parameter: method argument passed terra::distance() distance-based metrics (extent, maxlength, elongation). Area (terra::expanse()) perimeter (terra::perim()) use terra's built-CRS-dependent calculations: geodesic geographic (lon/lat) CRS, Cartesian projected CRS. method = "geo" "haversine" input projected CRS, geometry temporarily reprojected EPSG:4326 required downstream metrics. Size metrics: Area: geodesic default; handled according selected method. Perimeter: geodesic default; handled according selected method. East-west extent: \(\bar{D}_{EW} = \frac{d(NW, NE) + d(SW, SE)}{2}\). North-south extent: \(\bar{D}_{NS} = \frac{d(SW, NW) + d(SE, NE)}{2}\). Maximum length (Feret diameter): \(L_{\max} = \max_{p_i, p_j} d(p_i, p_j)\). Shape metrics: Compactness (Polsby-Popper): area normalized perimeter, relative circle: \(C = \frac{4\pi }{P^2}\). Reock compactness: \(R = \frac{}{A_{MEC}}\). minimum enclosing circle computed local Lambert azimuthal equal-area projection centred feature (GEOS hulls planar), measured back input's CRS. Shape index (perimeter relative circle equal area): \(SI = \frac{P}{2\sqrt{\pi }}\). Circularity ratio: \(CR = \frac{4A}{\pi L_{\max}^2}\). Fractal dimension (FRAGSTATS convention; approaches 1 simple, square-like shapes 2 highly convoluted boundaries): \(D = \frac{2 \ln(0.25 P)}{\ln()}\). Sinuosity: \(S = \frac{P}{L_{\max}}\). Orientation metrics: Bearing: orientation longest axis; computed geographic coordinates needed. Northerness: \(N = \cos(\text{bearing} \times \frac{\pi}{180})\). Elongation: ratio major minor axis minimum bounding rectangle. Elongation calculated ratio mean two largest side lengths mean two shortest side lengths: \(E = \frac{\text{mean}(\text{long sides})}{\text{mean}(\text{short sides})}\). Hole part metrics: Hole area percentage, relative gross area (including holes): \(HA\% = \frac{A_{\text{holes}}}{+ A_{\text{holes}}} \times 100\). num_holes, hole_area, num_polygons direct counts/areas derived polygon topology.

title: Find largest distance between a pair of opposite vertices — get_distant_points
text: v SpatVector object representing polygon, pre-computed convex hull isHull = TRUE. isHull Logical. TRUE, v treated pre-computed convex hull. FALSE (default), convex hull computed internally. distance Logical indicating whether return maximum distance (default TRUE). bearing Logical indicating whether return bearing (default TRUE). output Character string. "points" (default) returns point geometry outputs. "value" returns numeric metric values , "polygon" returns input geometry requested metric columns added. by_feature Logical. FALSE (default), compute single response convex hull whole input set. TRUE, compute one response per polygon feature. method Character string passed terra::distance(). Defaults "geo" (recommended). supported options "haversine" "cosine". three lon/lat great-circle methods; projected CRS, method ignored distances Cartesian. Bearing computed geographic coordinates needed.

title: Find largest distance between a pair of opposite vertices — get_distant_points
text: output = "points", list containing: south_point SpatVector southernmost point north_point SpatVector northernmost point distance Maximum distance meters (distance = TRUE) bearing Axial orientation: geographic bearing southernmost northernmost point, degrees within [-90, 90] (bearing = TRUE). pair always ordered south north, describes orientation longest axis, travel direction: -90/90 east-west, 0 north-south. output = "value", returns numeric scalar one metric requested, named numeric vector requested. output = "polygon", returns input geometry requested metric columns added. by_feature = TRUE, returns per-feature outputs (list, numeric vector/data.frame, polygon columns, depending output).

title: Find largest distance between a pair of opposite vertices — get_distant_points
text: Distances convex-hull vertex pairs evaluated terra::distance() using selected method, returned pair true geodesic maximum (hulls small, exhaustive search cheap). earlier rotating-calipers implementation searched antipodal pairs planar coordinate space, miss geodesic maximum lon/lat data. Tie-breaking & Point Ordering: multiple antipodal pairs share maximum distance, ties broken selecting pair containing southernmost (westernmost) coordinate. points ordered output : south_point (point 1): southernmost (westernmost, case tie) point pair. north_point (point 2): northernmost (easternmost) point pair. geographic bearing calculated south_point north_point using geosphere::bearing(). needed, geometry internally transformed geographic coordinates bearing calculation.

title: geomattR 0.3.0
text: Accuracy improvements geodesic workflows. Values reock, elongation_rectangle maxlength may change lon/lat input, especially high latitudes: minimum enclosing circle (reock) minimum bounding rectangle (elongation_rectangle) now computed local Lambert azimuthal equal-area projection centred feature, instead raw lon/lat degrees. GEOS hull constructions planar, minimizing degree space distorted “minimum” geometry wherever degree longitude shorter degree latitude. hull measured back input’s CRS. maxlength (distance/bearing outputs get_distant_points()) now found evaluating convex-hull vertex pairs geodesically single vectorised terra::distance() call. previous rotating-calipers candidate search operated planar coordinate space miss true geodesic maximum. internal rotating-calipers helper removed. Performance packaging: calculate_geometric_attributes() gains vectorised fast path area, perimeter, decimallongitude /decimallatitude requested: terra’s multi-feature methods called instead looping per feature. by_feature branches calc_extent(), calc_elongation() get_distant_points() longer compute (discard) convex hull entire input set. NAMESPACE now uses targeted importFrom() declarations instead blanket import(terra) / import(methods); two previously unqualified subset() / aggregate() calls now terra::-qualified.

title: geomattR 0.2.0
text: Breaking changes documented metric contracts: bearing now documented axial orientation [-90, 90] degrees: maximum-length line always oriented southernmost northernmost endpoint, values outside range unreachable. 0 = north-south axis, -90/90 = east-west axis. Computed values unchanged. northerness = cos(bearing) now documented range [0, 1]; negative values unreachable. fractaldimension now follows FRAGSTATS convention 2 * log(0.25 * P) / log() (McGarigal & Marks 1995, doi:10.2737/PNW-GTR-351). Values change relative previous 2 * log(P) / log(), fall outside [1, 2] small polygons. hole_area_pct now uses gross area (including holes) denominator, matching documentation. Values change relative previous net-area denominator. decimallongitude / decimallatitude now always decimal degrees: centroid reprojected EPSG:4326 input CRS projected. Previously, method = "cosine" projected CRS returned metres column names. fixes improvements: Documentation longer describes method = "cosine" “planar CRS”. geo, haversine cosine lon/lat great-circle methods terra::distance(); projected CRS argument ignored distances Cartesian. calc_elongation() computes rectangle side lengths explicitly unique corners ring order, instead relying undocumented ordering terra::crds() output, returns Inf degenerate (zero-width) rectangles instead failing dividing zero. Removed -op transform argument passed terra::expanse(); area geodesic lon/lat input Cartesian projected input. num_holes counted hole column terra::geom() instead length() fillHoles() result; num_polygons uses nrow(). New input validation: clear error zero-row inputs, warning invalid geometries, warning hull spans 180 degrees longitude (antimeridian), bounding-box extents unreliable.
